'''De-sparsified lasso''' contributes to construct confidence intervals and statistical tests for single or low-dimensional components of a large parameter vector in high-dimensional model.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Geer |first1=Sara van de |last2=Buhlmann |first2=Peter |last3=Ritov |first3=Ya'acov |last4=Dezeure |first4=Ruben |title=On Asymptotically Optimal Confidence Regions and Tests for High-Dimensional Models |journal=The Annals of Statistics |date=2014 |volume=42 |issue=3 |pages=1162–1202 |doi=10.1214/14-AOS1221 |arxiv=1303.0518 |s2cid=9663766 }}</ref>

==High-dimensional linear model==

<math> Y = X\beta^0 + \epsilon </math>
with <math> n \times p </math> design matrix <math>X =: [X_1,..., X_p]</math> (<math> n \times p</math> vectors <math>X_j</math>), <math>\epsilon \sim N_n(0, \sigma^2_\epsilon I)</math> independent of <math>X</math> and unknown regression <math>p \times 1</math> vector <math>\beta^0</math>.

The usual method to find the parameter is by Lasso:
<math> \hat{\beta}^n(\lambda) = \underset{\beta \in \mathbb{R} ^ p}{\arg\min} \ \frac{1}{2 n} \left\| Y - X \beta \right\| ^ 2 _ 2 + \lambda \left\| \beta \right\| _ 1. </math>

The de-sparsified lasso is a method modified from the Lasso estimator which fulfills the [[Karush–Kuhn–Tucker conditions]]<ref>{{cite web|last1=Tibshirani|first1=Ryan|last2=Gordon|first2=Geoff|title=Karush-Kuhn-Tucker conditions|url=https://www.cs.cmu.edu/~ggordon/10725-F12/slides/16-kkt.pdf}}</ref> is as follows:

<math>\hat{\beta}^n(\lambda,M) = \hat{\beta}^n(\lambda) + \frac{1}{n} M X^T(Y- X \hat{\beta}^n (\lambda)) </math>

where <math>M \in \mathbb{R}^{p\times p}</math> is an arbitrary matrix. The matrix <math>M</math> is generated using a surrogate inverse covariance matrix.

==Generalized linear model==

Desparsifying <math>l_1</math>-[[Field norm|norm]] penalized [[estimators]] and corresponding theory can also be applied to models with convex loss functions such as generalized linear models.

Consider the following <math>1 \times p</math> vectors of covariables <math>x_i \in \chi\subset \mathbb{R}^p</math> and univariate responses <math>y_i \in Y \subset R</math> for <math> i = 1,...,n</math>

we have a loss function 
<math>\rho_\beta(y,x) = \rho(y, x \beta) (\beta \in \mathbb{R}^p)</math>
which is assumed to be strictly [[convex function]] in <math>\beta \in \mathbb{R}^p.</math>

The <math>l_1</math>-norm regularized estimator is 
<math> \hat{\beta}=\underset{\beta}{\arg\min}(P_n \rho_\beta + \lambda\left\| \beta \right\|_1).</math>

Similarly, the [[Lasso]] for node wise [[regression analysis|regression]] with matrix input is defined as follows:
Denote by <math>\hat{\Sigma}</math> a matrix which we want to approximately invert using nodewise lasso.

The de-sparsified <math>l_1</math>-norm regularized estimator is as follows:
<math> \hat{\gamma_j}:= \underset{\gamma \in \mathbb{R}^{p-1}}{\arg\min}(\hat{\Sigma}_{j,j} - 2 \hat{\Sigma}_{j,/j} \gamma + \gamma^T \hat{\Sigma}_{/j,/j} \gamma + 2 \lambda_j\left\|\gamma\right\|_1</math>

where <math>\hat{\Sigma}_{j,/j}</math> denotes the <math>j</math>th row of <math>\hat{\Sigma}</math> without the diagonal element <math>(j,j)</math>, and <math>\hat{\Sigma}_{/j,/j}</math> is the sub matrix without the <math>j</math>th row and <math>j</math>th column.
